newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends weaker in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends weaker in range-bound trade.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended lower on light commission house selling offset by trade buying at the bottom of the range.
"There was a lack of follow-through from the funds," said one commission house broker. "We had some light commission house selling. The trade was doing some bargain hunting at the bottom."
The active October contract closed at 11.58 cents a lb, down 0.07 cents from Friday's close, in a range of 11.56 to 11.68 cents a lb.

One source noted that the speculative long position increased over the last two weeks in Commodity Futures Trading Commission's commitment of traders report. "The long position was expected to fall to 120,000 lots and instead it rose to 140,000 lots (from 132,915 lots two weeks ago)," he said.
"What that tells me is that there's a lot of stale longs in the market that will be looking for a selling opportunity," he said.
Anne Prendergast, analyst with Refco Inc, noted some trade buying at 11.55 cents in October and producer selling at the top of the range.
On the fundamental side of the market, "The possibility of crop damage as a result of El Nino is providing some underlying support," she said.
Other dealers noted that Brazillian exports continue to flow to the U.S. "That's where some of the hedge selling came from today," said one physical dealer.
